fullarm:
Context from a materials paper:
- Pristine g-C3N4 evolves little H2 under visible light; efficient metal-free photocatalysts are needed
- Introduce S dopants by loading molten sulfur into g-C3N4-E, then pyrolysing off the excess sulfur
- Hydrothermal treatment of g-C3N4-E with sulfur at 180 C gives sulfur-loaded S@g-C3N4-E
- Pyrolysis of S@g-C3N4-E at 520 C under N2 gives S-g-C3N4-E
- Sulfur is bonded into the heptazine framework as C-S-C (S on N sites) in S-g-C3N4-E
- S-doped (R-type) and S-free (O-type) domains in contact form an isotype S-scheme heterojunction with an internal field
- Internal field recombines O-domain CB electrons with R-domain VB holes, leaving R-domain electrons (-0.64 V) to reduce H+ and O-domain holes (2.25 V) to oxidise TEOA
- Photogenerated charges separate more efficiently and recombine less in S-g-C3N4-E than in g-C3N4 and g-C3N4-E

Panels:
- F8a: caption: Fig. 8 ... Photoluminescence spectra and | condition: Photoluminescence spectra and

Question: The claim under test is that photogenerated charges separate more efficiently and recombine less in S-g-C3N4-E than in g-C3N4 and g-C3N4-E. Panel F8a gives the photoluminescence spectra for all four labeled samples (g-C3N4, g-C3N4-E, S@g-C3N4-E, S-g-C3N4-E). Reading the panel together with what is otherwise known about these samples' photocurrent and H2 yield, does the PL data cleanly back this claim, or does it complicate the picture?

key.answer_key: The panel complicates it: S@g-C3N4-E also shows strongly quenched PL, with its peak at about 45% of the g-C3N4 peak, yet this sample has the lowest photocurrent and near-zero H2 yield (o25). So the panel's PL quenching does not track cleanly with better charge separation and higher photocatalytic performance across all four samples -- the simple story in the claim needs qualification.
key.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel (o25), which is the sole graded target for this trace.
